text: {"memo": "As of March 31, 2025, Netflix’s most recently completed fiscal year was 2024. In 2024, Netflix delivered revenue of about $39.0 billion, up roughly 13% from 2023, and net income of about $8.7 billion, or diluted EPS of about $23.1. Operating margin expanded to about 32%, and free cash flow was roughly $7.6 billion. Growth was driven by stronger paid membership, price increases, and a continued TV and film content slate. In 2023, revenue was about $34.6 billion, up 6.8% versus 2022, with net income of about $5.4 billion and EPS of about $13.7. Operating margin was about 26%. In 2022, revenue reached about $31.6 billion, up 16.8%, with net income of about $5.1 billion and EPS of about $15.3; operating margin was about 30%. Cash flow remained robust, though margins compressed in 2021 when the business was scaling. For the 2025 outlook, the March 31 tape would be cautious: 2024 results beat expectations, but 2025 guidance pointed to weaker first-quarter growth and margin normalization. The stock had rallied into 2025 on AI-driven ad confidence and live events. On balance, I would stay long Netflix into earnings, but size positions smaller given rich valuation and softer near-term growth."}
